description:
Advances: ancora.gate

Severity: High (calibrated). Regression introduced by ancora-rdx, already merged to main.

Concrete failure: mix test fails roughly 1 run in 3 with ExUnit.TimeoutError after 60000ms. Measured on main plus the ancora-p47 branch: run 1 green, run 2 = 2 failures (Ancora.Scaffold.FreshAdopterTest "fresh adopter goes from unanchored red to tagged green" and Mix.Tasks.Spec.PrimeTest "prime routes usage and environment failures without a verdict", both ExUnit.TimeoutError), run 3 green. The implementer on ancora-p47 hit the same thing independently.

Cause: test/support/ancora_case.exs:133 seed_build_path!/1 does File.cp_r!(Mix.Project.build_path(), build_path) on EVERY run_mix_subprocess call, and there are about 30 such calls per full run. That is roughly 135 MB of copying per suite. It was introduced by ancora-rdx to give each subprocess its own MIX_BUILD_PATH, which was correct in intent — the previous shared build path was a source of lock contention — but the per-call copy is expensive enough that under load a single subprocess test exceeds the 60 second ExUnit timeout.

Both graders saw the cost and rated it affordable. The cold verifier note read: "seed_build_path! does a File.cp_r! of _build/test (4.5 MB) on every subprocess call ... The suite still finishes in 32 seconds, so it is affordable now, but it is why the touched-file run alone takes 25 seconds and it will scale with _build." That judgement was wrong at the 1-in-3 rate now observed, and it is worth recording as a lesson: a cost flagged as affordable should be measured under repetition, not at one sample.

Fix direction (implementer choice, but do not simply raise the timeout — that hides it): seed ONE build path per suite or per test module and reuse it across subprocess calls, rather than copying per call. A hardlink or clone copy is another option on APFS. Whatever shape you choose, each subprocess must still not share a mutable build directory with a CONCURRENT one, which is the property ancora-rdx was buying.

Verification: full suite run 10 times consecutively with zero failures and no ExUnit.TimeoutError, on both CI matrix legs (Elixir 1.19.5/OTP 28.3.1 and 1.18.4/OTP 26.2.5). Report the wall-clock of each run so the improvement is visible. Do not weaken any assertion and do not raise the ExUnit timeout to pass.

Status note (2026-09-03, orchestrator Phase 0): the co-landing sentence below is stale. ancora-8t2 was closed as superseded and its CI fix folded into ancora-xla.5. ancora-p47 is already implemented on its own stage branch and awaiting cold verification. This ticket no longer has to ride either of them; it is the epic's own prerequisite.

Measured again on the ancora-xla epic worktree at base 5d9cb40 with no code changes: 331 tests, 7 failures, wall clock 210s against the 32s baseline this ticket records. Every failure was ExUnit.TimeoutError inside run_mix_subprocess, three of them the exact tests named above. Host load average was 162 on 10 cores at the time, so contention amplified the defect rather than causing it: the same test passes alone, but takes 28 seconds by itself, which is the _build copy cost and nothing else.

Verification:
- Tests to pass: the full suite, run 10 times consecutively with zero failures and no ExUnit.TimeoutError, on both CI matrix legs (Elixir 1.19.5/OTP 28.3.1 and 1.18.4/OTP 26.2.5). Report each run's wall clock so the improvement is visible. If host load is above roughly 2 per core, say so with the measured figure rather than reporting a number that load explains.
- Behaviors to demonstrate: (1) a subprocess mix run no longer copies the whole build path per call; (2) two concurrent subprocess tests still never share a mutable build directory, which is the isolation property ancora-rdx bought; (3) the single-test wall clock for test/ancora/scaffold/fresh_adopter_test.exs drops well below its current 28 seconds.
- Verification cadence:
  - Iteration tier: the three named timeout-prone files plus mix spec.validate; no full suite mid-iteration.
  - Final tier: immediately before IMPLEMENTED, run-until-green: mix compile --warnings-as-errors && mix test && mix format --check-formatted && mix deps.unlock --check-unused && mix spec.check --base the epic base sha recorded at admission. The 10-run repetition above is part of the final tier for this ticket specifically, because the defect is a frequency, not a single failure.
  - Verifier tier: the 10-run repetition and mix spec.check --base the epic base sha recorded at admission. This is the one ticket whose verifier does run the full suite, repeatedly; that repetition is the point.
- Standing bounce-class checks:
  - Do not raise the ExUnit timeout, do not weaken an assertion, and do not mark a test async: false to dodge the contention.
  - Fixture hygiene: one TmpGitRepo per test, no shared temp dirs, async only where the fixture allows.
  - Spec surfaces kept fresh for every touched callable surface. Drift, growth, and shrink clear only through substantive requirement or scenario edits in the same diff, never through a Spec-Ack trailer.
- proves: the suite is green ten times running, and each subprocess test still gets its own build directory.

Allowed touches (this ticket may modify):
- test/support/ancora_case.exs (seed_build_path!/1 and run_mix_subprocess/2)
- test/support/**
- test/test_helper.exs
- .spec/specs/ancora.gate.spec.md (acknowledgment edits only: substantive requirement or scenario updates that clear drift, growth, or shrink for this ticket's own changes; never weakening a must)

Out of Scope (files):
- lib/**
- .github/workflows/ci.yml (ancora-xla.5 owns it)
- mix.exs, VERSION, CHANGELOG.md

Out of Scope (intent):
- no raising the ExUnit timeout, globally or per test or per module
- no weakening or deleting an assertion to make a slow test pass
- no removing the per-subprocess build isolation that ancora-rdx introduced
- no production code changes; this is test infrastructure only

Merge gate:
- [ ] mix compile --warnings-as-errors
- [ ] mix test, ten consecutive green runs with wall clocks reported
- [ ] mix format --check-formatted
- [ ] mix deps.unlock --check-unused
- [ ] mix spec.check --base the epic base sha recorded at admission ends result=pass
- [ ] Scope check: diff touches only Allowed globs (mechanical)
- [ ] Auditor APPROVE comment on the ticket
title: Per-subprocess _build copy makes the suite time out about one run in three
